facts: Three brothers who had quarrelled with the complainant over a drain waited for him outside the temple. Two of them caught hold of his arms while the third struck him on the head with an iron rod. The medical report records a fracture of the skull. All three ran away together.

sections.title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention -
Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means

defenses.argument: The prosecution has failed to establish that the three brothers shared a 'common intention' to commit the assault; they merely acted in concert due to a pre-existing quarrel. The facts state they waited for the complainant and then attacked him, but there is no evidence of prior conspiracy or simultaneous intent to harm all three together at the specific moment of the assault. Without proof that the act was done 'in furtherance of the common intention of all,' Section 34 cannot be applied to hold them jointly liable.
defenses.fact_quote: Three brothers who had quarrelled with the complainant over a drain waited for him outside the temple. Two of them caught hold of his arms while the third struck him on the head with an iron rod.

defenses.argument: The essential ingredient of 'riot' under Section 148 is the formation of an unlawful assembly consisting of five or more persons, which is not present in these facts. The prosecution relies on only three brothers acting together, which legally constitutes a joint offence but does not satisfy the statutory threshold for rioting.

The prosecution has failed to prove that the accused acted 'voluntarily' or with 'intention' to cause grievous hurt. The facts only state that an iron rod was used and a fracture occurred; they do not establish the accused's subjective intent to inflict injury, nor do they rule out self-defence or negligence as possible explanations for the injury sustained.
